understanding: Verify IER shows all interrupts disabled after reset with value 00h and bits 7-4 remain zero via masked Wishbone read.
preconditions: WAIT for t_bringup_clk reset coordination completed before Wishbone read
Clock stable and wishbone_bus idle and ready for register access
Use symbolic SYM_IER_ADDR for IER access without inventing bus value
stimulus_steps: WAIT for t_bringup_clk reset deassertion completion
READ IER via wishbone_bus at SYM_IER_ADDR yielding IER_RDATA [f_ier_reset_value]
check_steps: COMPARE (IER_RDATA AND 0xFF) TO 0x00 for all-disabled reset [f_ier_disabled, f_ier_reset_value]
COMPARE (IER_RDATA AND 0xF0) TO 0x00 for reserved bits 7-4 remain zero [f_ier_reserved_zero]
USE explicit masks 0xFF and 0xF0 with expected 0x00 and null mirror unknown; never invent zero for unknown
completion: DECLARE pass iff both masked compares match with zero scoreboard mismatches
ENFORCE TEST_TIMEOUT_CYCLES as testbench operational limit not DUT timing

facts.statement: Upon reset all interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.
facts.quote: All interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.

facts.statement: IER reset value is 00h with all enables disabled.
IER bits 7-4 are Reserved and Should be logic 0.

questions: What is the expected WISHBONE write and read behavior for IER bits 7-4 when written to 1, including whether they are stored, returned on read, or affect interrupt generation?
